clue.text: Endless humour leading to proper disappointment

indicators.note: endless asks for the word for humour with its final letter dropped

parts.note: comedy is humour
own in the sense of one's proper or particular, as in 'his own room'

explanation.surface: A joke that fizzles out leaves a properly deflated audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts the last letter from COMEDY to leave COMED, and OWN follows it ('leading to').
explanation.definitionFit: A fall from expectation or status is a letdown, a disappointment.

clue.text: Start up in business (beginning, not end, of November)

indicators.note: the first letter of November takes the place of its last letter in the word for business

parts.note: commerce is trade or business

explanation.surface: Someone launches a business venture at the start of November.
explanation.walkthrough: November begins with N and ends with R, so the R of COMMERCE gives way to N.
explanation.definitionFit: To start up something is to begin it, a synonym.

clue.text: Service by European practitioner

parts.note: Mass is a church service
Eur is an abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A doctor from Europe provides a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like the practitioner's work, but it is the church service, MASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur is a practitioner of therapeutic rubbing and kneading of muscles.

clue.text: North African governor accepts Italian god

indicators.note: accepts means the governor's title takes the next letter inside it

parts.note: a dey was the title of the Ottoman governor of Algiers, Tunis or Tripoli
Italian gives IT

explanation.surface: An Algerian ruler welcomes an Italian deity into his court.
explanation.definitionFit: A deity is a divine being, synonymous with a god.

clue.text: Check a tower in a storm -it shows which way the wind's blowing

definitions.text: it shows which way the wind's blowing

indicators.note: a storm throws things about, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Inspect a tower during a gale and see which way the wind blows.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CHECK A TOWER are rearranged ('in a storm').
explanation.definitionFit: A vane in the shape of a rooster on a roof turns to point into the wind.

clue.text: Mind being cornered by tipsy chemist

indicators.note: the answer is trapped inside the words that surround it, as if cornered

explanation.surface: A drunk pharmacist has someone's mind trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across tiPSY CHEmist, held in ('cornered') by the surrounding letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Psyche is the soul or mind, as in psychology.

clue.text: Prophet entertaining two graduates -no big deal

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them within, so the prophet's word goes round the others

parts.note: a seer is a prophet
an MA is a Master of Arts graduate
an LLB is a Bachelor of Laws graduate

explanation.surface: A prophet hosting two university graduates finds it no big deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The two graduates are MA and LLB, put inside SEER ('entertaining'): S + MA LLB + EER.
explanation.definitionFit: Small beer is a British idiom for something trivial or unimportant.

clue.text: Cube's odd contour

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of contour are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the strange outline of a cube.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CONTOUR are rearranged ('odd'); 'Cube's' reads as 'Cube is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a small cube of fried or toasted bread.

clue.text: Still found former abstainer imbibing contents of cans

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the abstainer's letters take others inside

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes an abstainer from alcohol

indicators.note: contents means the inside of the word, without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An ex-teetotaller is still found drinking from cans.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of 'cans' is AN; TT 'imbibing' it gives TANT after EX.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extant still exists, so it can still be found.

clue.text: Disastrous calamity's not a secret

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so these letters are thrown into a new order
not signals that the letter a is left out of the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A dreadful calamity is no secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove an A from CALAMITYS ('not a') and rearrange the rest ('Disastrous').
explanation.definitionFit: Mystical means having hidden spiritual meaning, esoteric or secret.

clue.text: Arrangement of artwork by non-professional is unacceptable

parts.note: lay means amateur, not of a profession, as in a layman
out means not allowed or unacceptable, as in 'that's out'

explanation.surface: An amateur's artwork arrangement is rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link: LAY then OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A layout is the design and arrangement of text and images on a page.

clue.text: Each night goes on line

indicators.note: goes on means the first piece is placed before the next

parts.note: eve is the night or evening before an event
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Every night someone goes online.
explanation.walkthrough: EVE comes first and RY follows ('goes on').
explanation.definitionFit: Every and each both refer to all members of a group one by one.

clue.text: Form of hut with finial, very grandiose

indicators.note: a form of something is a version of it, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Putting a finial on a humble hut makes it very grand.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of HUT and FINIAL are rearranged ('Form of'). A finial is an ornament on top of a roof or spire.
explanation.definitionFit: Hifalutin means pompous or pretentious, putting on grand airs.

clue.text: They'll give a sharp reaction if pressed

definitions.text: They'll give a sharp reaction if pressed

parts.words: They'll give a sharp reaction if pressed
parts.note: a reading of people reacting badly under pressure, but really pressing a button releases a spring-loaded blade

explanation.surface: Some people snap when pushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp reaction' sounds like a snappy temper; press the button and the blade springs out.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring-loaded pocket blades open with a sharp action when their button is pressed.

clue.text: Homer accompanied by a set of notes?

definitions.text: Homer accompanied by a set of notes?

parts.words: Homer accompanied by a set of notes?
parts.note: suggests the Greek poet set to music, but a homer is a homing bird that flies with messages attached

explanation.surface: Someone imagines the epic poet set to music.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'homer' is a homing bird; the 'notes' are messages, not music.
explanation.definitionFit: A homing bird trained to fly with written messages tied to its leg.

clue.text: Cross, one bishop's taken on board when circumnavigating isle

indicators.note: to circumnavigate is to go all the way round, so the outer letters surround the next
taken on means the bishop's letters join onto the front of the board's

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title
a table is a board, as in board and lodging
I is an abbreviation for isle, as on maps

explanation.surface: An angry passenger: a bishop has been taken aboard a ship sailing round an island.
explanation.walkthrough: I + RR + TABLE go round ('circumnavigating') another I: IRR + I + TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross as an adjective means annoyed or bad-tempered.

clue.text: Gentlemen mostly fidget in bishop's office, on reflection

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other
a reflection reverses an image, so the word for bishop's office is read backwards

parts.note: a see is the seat or office of a bishop

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to squirm is to fidget

explanation.surface: Gentlemen in a bishop's office fidget while thinking things over.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE reversed ('on reflection') is EES; SQUIRM without its end ('mostly') is SQUIR, put 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Esquire is a title of courtesy given to gentlemen.

clue.text: People crashing into barn-doors, perhaps, wide features of the countryside?

indicators.note: into means the people's word goes inside the rearranged letters
crashing suggests wreckage, so the letters of barn-doors are scattered

parts.note: folk means people

explanation.surface: People smash into barn doors in rural landscapes.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNDOORS is rearranged ('crashing') to NOR BROADS, with FOLK put 'into' it. The Norfolk Broads are a network of rivers and lakes in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The navigable shallow lakes of eastern England are broad water features in the countryside; 'wide' plays on broads.

clue.text: Bits of pasta -lots will be covered with Parmesan, ultimately

indicators.note: in a down answer, being covered means having that letter placed on top
ultimately points to the final letter of Parmesan

parts.note: oodles means lots, plenty

explanation.surface: A plate of pasta heaped with Parmesan cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the last letter of Parmesan ('ultimately'), sits on top ('covered with') of OODLES in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles are strips of pasta.

clue.text: Food, source of calcium worker's consumed

indicators.note: consumed means eaten up, so the worker's letters swallow the other piece

parts.note: an ant is the crossword's usual worker
lime, from limestone, is a source of calcium

explanation.surface: A worker eats some calcium-rich food.
explanation.walkthrough: LIME goes inside ANT ('consumed'), with 'worker's' read as 'worker has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for nourishment or food.

clue.text: Means of calculating, mostly, back in Australia

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: In Australia, people often count backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' without its last letter ('mostly') is BAC, put 'in' AUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads used to do sums.

clue.text: A gift for literature

parts.note: sounds like a talent for writing, but means a present that buys reading matter

explanation.surface: Someone has a natural flair for writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gift' means talent on the surface, but here it is a present exchangeable for books.
explanation.definitionFit: A voucher given as a present that can be exchanged in a shop for a book.

clue.text: Vale in France

parts.note: suggests a French valley, but vale is the Latin farewell, so this asks for the French goodbye

explanation.surface: A valley somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vale' looks like a valley; it is the Latin for farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word of farewell, equivalent to Latin vale.

clue.text: About to be in time for match

indicators.note: to be in means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: an age is a period of time
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is about to arrive in time for the match.
explanation.walkthrough: RE goes inside AGE ('to be in').
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to match or correspond, as in two accounts that tally.

clue.text: Famous people taking Ecstasy out in Indonesian island

indicators.note: taking with out signals a letter is removed
out completes the instruction that the drug's letter is taken out of the island

parts.note: Celebes is the former name of Sulawesi, an Indonesian island
E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: Celebrities taking Ecstasy on an Indonesian island.
explanation.walkthrough: One E is removed from CELEBES ('taking ... out').
explanation.definitionFit: Celebs is short for celebrities, people who are well known.

clue.text: Bowler's contribution, to try for catch

parts.note: in cricket, a bowler delivers an over of six balls
to hear a case is to try it in court

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler does his bit, trying for a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler in cricket; a judge hears or tries a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a remark accidentally is to overhear it.

clue.text: Cricket team from American ship in VI?

indicators.note: in means the ship's letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals, and sex is Latin for six
USS, United States Ship, prefixes American naval vessels

explanation.surface: A cricket team travels on an American ship among six.
explanation.walkthrough: VI is the Roman numeral for six, which is SEX in Latin. Sussex is an English county with a first-class cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sussex County Cricket Club is one of the English county sides.

clue.text: Beast swallowing choicest bit of organic substance now seen as health hazard

definitions.text: substance now seen as health hazard

indicators.note: swallowing means the animal's letters take the rest inside them

parts.note: an ass is a beast of burden
best means choicest

indicators.note: a bit of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An animal eats the best part of some organic matter that is now thought harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: BEST plus O, the first letter of organic ('bit of'), go inside ASS ('swallowing').
explanation.definitionFit: A fibrous mineral once used for insulation, now known to cause lung disease.
